title: Measure the profiler and SIMD candidates on our hot paths
summary: An available sampling profiler (perf 6.8.12) was run on one named hot path, the native scalar CRF core of the parse route. The measured bound is data-structure / pointer-chasing (BTreeMap key search ~24.6% of self time, sparse_weight reads), not a dense contiguous numeric kernel, and the hardware counters show low branch and L1 miss rates with a latency component (IPC 1.53, backend-idle 12.2%). Per-candidate verdicts: hotpath-rs = defer (the profiler's distinctive async/lock/channel signal was not measurable on a synchronous CPU path); fearless-simd = reject for the identified hot paths (no dense numeric loop; the dominant cost is BTreeMap/sparse lookups that vectorization cannot address). No dependency was added to any manifest and Cargo.lock is untouched.

knowledge_base_sources.note: Adjacent knowledge base entry describing hotpath 0.28 (feature-gated Rust profiler + TUI + Prometheus + MCP).
Adjacent knowledge base entry describing the 2026 SIMD ladder and fearless-simd 1.0 (stable, Sep 2026).

hot_paths.name: Parse route / native scalar CRF core
hot_paths.why_hot: The native CRF decode runs once per segmentation span over frozen Wapiti models; the in-process receipt attributes 97% of the four measured phases to viterbi_decode for the fulltext family. It is the compute kernel of the native parse route shadow (ADR-076).
hot_paths.existing_instrumentation: None at function level. The Java parse route carries a per-call tracing span (crates/da-parse/src/parser.rs:131, name="grobid_parse", ADR-052) and the native core carries an in-process observational phase receipt (native_core_profile.rs) with wall-clock shares only.

hot_paths.name: Replay and materialization path
hot_paths.why_hot: Always-run side-effect boundary after a verified cache hit; writes Entity nodes and MENTIONS/FOUND_IN edges to the HOT graph store in a per-entity loop (crates/da-application/src/extraction.rs:168-260).
hot_paths.existing_instrumentation: No dedicated span. The outer extract_from_parsed span (crates/da-application/src/extraction.rs:123, name="extract") times the extractor call and the materialization together, so the two halves are not separated.
hot_paths.measurement_note: Not profiled in this task: no hermetic in-memory runner for this path exists in the example surface (no da-cli example uses MockGraphStore). Named as worth instrumenting; a profile is the measurement that would inform a hotpath-rs adoption for this surface.

hot_paths.name: Embedding call
hot_paths.why_hot: Called once per entity/section enrichment against the fd_api bge-m3 HTTP service; latency is dominated by the remote round trip, not local math.
hot_paths.existing_instrumentation: None. kg-* crates intentionally carry zero tracing dependency (AGENTS.md logging section), so the HTTP boundary is only visible to da-adapters/da-application callers.
hot_paths.measurement_note: Not profiled in this task: the call is network-bound against an external service (http://127.0.0.1:8000) and is not a hermetic CPU target.

instrument.name: perf
instrument.kind: sampling profiler with hardware performance counters
instrument.note: perf is the sampling profiler already available on the host; it measures what the existing stage-level tracing spans cannot: function-level attribution and hardware counters. It is used here as the measurement instrument because adopting a new profiler dependency is out of scope for this task.

runs.command: perf record -F 999 -g -o /tmp/m516_perf.data -- target/debug/examples/native_core_profile --artifact /tmp/m516_perf_ncp.json --rows 256 && perf report --stdio -i /tmp/m516_perf.data --no-children --sort symbol

measurement.counter_caveat: 11 hardware events were multiplexed at roughly 40% per-counter coverage, so absolute counts are scaled estimates; IPC is a within-group ratio and the branch/cache/L1 percentages are ratios, so the qualitative bound (compute vs memory vs data-structure) is robust.

measured_bound.classification: data-structure / latency, not dense numeric compute
measured_bound.evidence: The single largest self-time consumers are BTreeMap key search (find_key_index 16.65% + search_tree 5.54% + BTreeMap<u32,f64>::get 2.40% = 24.59%), which is pointer-chasing over a sparse map (CrfModel.weights: BTreeMap<usize, f64>, scalar_crf.rs:27) plus the per-call rebuild of a BTreeMap<&str, usize> lookup in map_input (scalar_crf.rs:342). viterbi_decode arithmetic is 14.40% self. Branch misses are 0.28% and L1-dcache misses 0.06%, so the cost is not memory-bandwidth and not branch misprediction; backend-idle 12.20% and IPC 1.53 indicate a dependency/latency component inside the lookup chains.
measured_bound.off_cpu_note: The profiled workload is synchronous and single-threaded (0.999 CPUs utilized); there is no async wait, Mutex contention, or channel queue depth on this path, so off-CPU attribution was not applicable here.

what_existing_instrumentation_did_not_me: Function-level attribution inside a stage: the ADR-052 tracing spans record per-stage wall time (grobid_parse, extract, batch_ingest) but cannot say which functions consume it. perf attributed BTreeMap key search at 24.59%, viterbi_decode at 14.40% and sparse_weight at 2.28% - the tracing layer collapses all of these into one span duration.

Compute-vs-memory bound: tracing has no hardware-counter notion, so it cannot distinguish a compute-bound loop from a memory-bound or data-structure-bound one. perf supplied IPC 1.53, branch-miss 0.28%, L1-dcache miss 0.06% and backend-idle 12.20%, which is what classifies the bound as data-structure/latency rather than dense compute.

Setup vs steady state: perf attributed 21.43% of samples to serde_yaml model/manifest parsing, which is one-time setup inside the profile process; a stage span would blend that into the stage's single duration.

candidates.name: hotpath-rs 0.28
candidates.kind: feature-gated Rust profiler (functions/allocations/CPU/async channels/locks/SQL/HTTP/IO/Tokio) with TUI, Prometheus and an MCP server
measured_basis: The one hot path that was profiled is synchronous and single-threaded (0.999 CPUs utilized, no async wait, no lock contention, no channel pressure). perf measured a data-structure-bound CPU loop, which is exactly the surface where hotpath-rs's distinctive features (async wait vs CPU attribution, Mutex/RwLock wait time and contention, mpsc queue depth, Tokio worker scheduling, SQL attribution) would report nothing.
hotpath-rs's SQL mode targets sqlx and Diesel; neither is present in the workspace (grep of Cargo.toml files finds no sqlx/Diesel), so that feature is inert here.

The existing tracing substrate already records per-stage wall-clock durations with semantic identity (ADR-052) and the governor already consumes gsd_exec evidence; the unmeasured delta is contention/off-CPU attribution, not raw duration.
The hosted hotpath Cloud option is rejected on egress grounds (no external egress); only the local TUI/static-report/MCP modes would be considered.
what_it_would_add_over_measured_instrume: Off-CPU async wait vs CPU-bound attribution that perf cannot separate by semantic unit (task/channel/lock).
Per-Mutex/RwLock wait time and contention - relevant because the Samyama HOT store and batch pipeline use locks and channels.
Live mpsc channel queue depth and Tokio worker scheduling.
An MCP endpoint an agent can query live, complementing the governor's static evidence store.
candidates.decision_changing_measurement: Profile a live long-running async path - `da serve-graph` (crates/kg-storage RemoteGraphStore read plane) under concurrent `da graph-ping`, or `da batch-ingest` over the catalog - and measure the fraction of wall time spent in off-CPU async wait or Mutex/RwLock contention that is invisible to the existing tracing spans. If that fraction is material (working threshold: >= 5% of wall time attributable to a named lock or channel, or a queue depth that grows under load), adopt with that measurement as justification; if the wait/contention fraction is negligible, close the candidate as not-justified.
rejected_alternatives: adopt now - rejected: it would add optional dependencies plus a runtime metrics server before any measurement shows the async/lock/channel signal the tool uniquely exposes.
guardrails: Adopting is out of scope for this task; no feature flag, dependency, or server was added.
Any future adoption must stay local (no egress to hotpath Cloud) and be feature-gated so the production build keeps zero instrumentation overhead.

candidates.name: fearless-simd 1.0 (stable, September 2026)
candidates.kind: portable SIMD library: safe access to intrinsics generic over vector width, with multiversioning
candidates.verdict_scope: the currently identified hot paths (parse-route native CRF core, replay/materialization, embedding call)
candidates.reason: No profiled hot path is dense numeric compute. On the one path that was profiled, the measured bound is data-structure and pointer-chasing: BTreeMap key search is 24.59% of self time (find_key_index + search_tree + BTreeMap<u32,f64>::get) and the decoder reads sparse weights (scalar_crf.rs sparse_weight -> CrfModel.weights: BTreeMap<usize, f64>, 2.28% self), while viterbi_decode arithmetic is 14.40% self with 0.28% branch misses and 0.06% L1-dcache misses. Portable SIMD vectorizes dense contiguous numeric loops; it cannot vectorize BTreeMap lookups or sparse weight reads, so it does not address the measured bottleneck. The two unprofiled paths are also not dense compute: the replay/materialization path is graph-store I/O and the embedding call is an HTTP round trip to fd_api. The project's own gate already encodes the same conclusion: crate::layout_runtime::gate_simd_candidate refuses MeasuredRetained unless a dense numeric kernel with semantic equality and repeated CPU improvement is proven, and the committed artifacts/parse_compat/native_core_profile.json disposition is measured_rejected with selection_forbidden=true and pgo_disposition=not_adopted.

measured_basis.note: Even though AVX2 is present, the harness measured a data-structure-bound loop, not a dense arithmetic loop.

candidates.reopen_condition: A measured dense contiguous numeric kernel would reopen the candidate: profile a loop whose self time is dominated by contiguous f32/f64 or integer arithmetic (not map lookups) and show it is a material share of a hot path, then build a bounded scalar-vs-SIMD candidate that passes a semantic-equality oracle plus a repeated CPU-improvement measurement through gate_simd_candidate before any selection. No such loop exists in the profiled surface today.
rejected_alternatives: adopt now - rejected: adds a dependency with no measured basis on any identified hot path.

vectorize the viterbi_decode loop speculatively - rejected: profiling before vectorization shows the loop's cost is dominated by BTreeMap/sparse lookups, not arithmetic, so vectorization would not move the measured bottleneck.
attribute the workload as memory-bandwidth bound - rejected: L1-dcache load misses are 0.06%, so the cost is not bandwidth; it is lookup dependency latency.

standards_context.isa_ladder: scalar -> autovectorization -> portable SIMD -> raw intrinsics
standards_context.avx2_note: AVX2 is partly emulated on many x86 parts and ~15% of x86 CPUs in 2026 lack it; the host has avx/avx2 and no avx512.
standards_context.math_note: The knowledge base notes autovectorization for float is largely a no-go on stable and recommends profiling first, which this task did.

diagnostics.note: The example writes the committed artifact path by default; pass --artifact to a temp path so artifacts/parse_compat/native_core_profile.json is not rewritten.

next_actions.finding: map_input rebuilds a BTreeMap<&str, usize> lookup over the whole observation table on every call (crates/da-domain/src/scalar_crf.rs:342), and CrfModel.weights is a BTreeMap<usize, f64> read sparsely (crates/da-domain/src/scalar_crf.rs:27, sparse_weight). The profile attributes 24.59% of self time to BTreeMap search.
next_actions.opportunity: A data-structure change (prebuilt/SortedVec or hash index, hoisted out of the per-call rebuild) is the measured lever on this hot path - no new dependency required. da-domain is functionally frozen and any change requires its own proof/slice; this is recorded as a finding, not adopted here.

next_actions.finding: materialize_extracted has no dedicated span; the outer extract span times extractor and materialization together.
next_actions.opportunity: Add an inner tracing span around the materialization loop so the replay/materialization path becomes measurable without a new profiler.

next_actions.finding: hotpath-rs's distinctive signal (async wait / lock contention / channel depth) is unmeasured.
next_actions.opportunity: Profile the live async pipeline as specified in the decision_changing_measurement before any adoption decision.
